decisions.reason: As a low-cost complementary care product in a growing flooring business, the cleaning soap keeps a useful option open with little downside while market acceptance is still being learned.
The maintenance oil extends the firm's established wood-floor care system and is inexpensive to keep available, so real-options logic favors waiting for more sales evidence rather than exiting early.

Because this care product serves the narrower oiled-floor segment, uncertainty is somewhat higher, but the cost of continuing is likely modest and the strategic fit is strong enough to retain it for now.
A moisture-protection underlay supports the core flooring offer and installation performance, so keeping it on the market preserves cross-selling value while demand information is still developing.

Although high-density underlay foam is more exposed to commodity-style competition, it still complements the flooring system and does not yet justify abandonment after only a short time on the market.

The oak parquet floor is close to the firm's core business and strategic growth path, and despite somewhat higher inventory and production commitment, one year is too early to give up the option absent clear failure signals.
